I will keep all 3.0 mu in cotton this year. I have farmed for 50 years, I am alone in the household, and I have a well, so I will choose a management plan that is steady, familiar, and not too labor-heavy. At the start of the season, I will use improved cotton seed rather than traditional seed because I want better stand establishment and more stable yield on my small plot. I will prepare the land with rotary tillage because it is easier for me to manage than deep ploughing and it fits a small cotton field well. For fertilizer, I will use a moderate rate: enough nitrogen to support vegetative growth, phosphorus to help roots and early growth, and potassium to support boll development. Since I have well irrigation, I will irrigate several key times rather than too often, mainly around establishment, budding, flowering, and boll setting if moisture is short. I will spray pesticides only as needed but I expect several applications because cotton usually faces insect pressure during the season. My goal is a stable yield with manageable labor, not the most aggressive input plan.
